   294	/-- Absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula for `N₂(θ)²`
   295	on `(0,∞)² × ℝ^d`. -/
   296	theorem N2integrand_integrable (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   297	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ)
   298	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   299	    Integrable (N2integrand (d := d) a θ) (P2.prod μ) := by
   300	  have hG := (FK_integrable μ hR a θ ha0 ha1 hθ).integral_prod_right
   301	  have hae : (fun yz : Rd d × (ℝ × ℝ) => ∫ l, FK a θ (l, yz) ∂L0) =ᵐ[μ.prod P2]
   302	      fun yz => N2integrand a θ (yz.2, yz.1) := by
   303	    filter_upwards [Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.ae ae_P2] with yz hyz
   304	    exact integral_FK_eq a θ ha0 yz.1 yz.2 hyz.2.2
   305	  exact (hG.congr hae).swap

   307	/-- The outer integrand of `N₂(θ)²` is integrable on `(0,∞)²`, so `N2sq` is a
   308	genuine (finite) integral. -/
   309	theorem N2_outer_integrable (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   310	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ)
   311	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   312	    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Real.exp (-(θ * (p.1 + p.2))) * |p.1 - p.2| ^ (-a) *
   313	      ∫ ξ, waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ ∂μ) P2 := by
   314	  refine (N2integrand_integrable μ hR a θ ha0 ha1 hθ).integral_prod_left.congr
   315	    (Eventually.of_forall fun p => ?_)
   316	  simp only [N2integrand]
   317	  rw [integral_const_mul]

   319	/-- The integrand of `N₁(θ)` is integrable on `(0,∞)`, given the homogeneity. -/
   320	theorem N1_integrable {alpha : ℝ} (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   321	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hthr : a + alpha < 2) :
   322	    Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0 := by
   323	  have hR1 : 0 ≤ resolvent μ 1 := integral_nonneg fun ξ => by positivity
   324	  have heq : (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) =ᵐ[L0]
   325	      fun l => l ^ (a - 1) * ((θ + l) ^ (alpha - 2) * resolvent μ 1) := by
   326	    filter_upwards [ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   327	    rw [resolvent_homog hI (θ + l) (by linarith)]
   328	  refine Integrable.congr ?_ heq.symm
   329	  refine integrable_of_rpow_bounds (a - 1) (a + alpha - 3)
   330	    (resolvent μ 1 * (θ ^ (alpha - 2) + 1)) (by linarith) (by linarith)
   331	    (by fun_prop : Measurable fun l : ℝ =>
   332	      l ^ (a - 1) * ((θ + l) ^ (alpha - 2) * resolvent μ 1)).aestronglyMeasurable ?_ ?_
   333	  · intro l hl _
   334	    have hp := Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le (a - 1)
   335	    have hq : (θ + l) ^ (alpha - 2) ≤ θ ^ (alpha - 2) :=
   336	      Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos hθ (by linarith) (by linarith)
   337	    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
   338	    have hθp := Real.rpow_nonneg hθ.le (alpha - 2)
   339	    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hq (mul_nonneg hp hR1)]
   340	  · intro l hl
   341	    have hl0 : 0 < l := lt_trans zero_lt_one hl
   342	    have hq : (θ + l) ^ (alpha - 2) ≤ l ^ (alpha - 2) :=
   343	      Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos hl0 (by linarith) (by linarith)
   344	    have hp := Real.rpow_nonneg hl0.le (a - 1)
   345	    have he : l ^ (a + alpha - 3) = l ^ (a - 1) * l ^ (alpha - 2) := by
   346	      rw [← Real.rpow_add hl0]; ring_nf
   347	    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity), he]
   348	    have hθp := Real.rpow_nonneg hθ.le (alpha - 2)
   349	    have hlp := Real.rpow_nonneg hl0.le (alpha - 2)
   350	    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hq (mul_nonneg hp hR1),
   351	      mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hR1 hθp) (mul_nonneg hp hlp)]

   353	/-- Finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 766-846) with the
   354	manuscript's hypothesis `H:homog` (temporal exponent `a = α₀`) and the supplied
   355	spectral homogeneity: for every `θ > 0` the spectral formula for `N₂(θ)²` is
   356	absolutely integrable on `(0,∞)² × ℝ^d`, its outer integrand is integrable on
   357	`(0,∞)²`, and the integrand of `N₁(θ)` is integrable on `(0,∞)`. -/
   358	theorem damped_norms_finite_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   359	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha)
   360	    (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   361	    Integrable (N2integrand (d := d) alpha0 θ) (P2.prod μ) ∧
   362	      Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Real.exp (-(θ * (p.1 + p.2))) * |p.1 - p.2| ^ (-alpha0) *
   363	        ∫ ξ, waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ ∂μ) P2 ∧
   364	      Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (alpha0 - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0 := by
   365	  have := h.μ_radon
   366	  have ha2 : alpha < 2 := by linarith [h.threshold, h.alpha0_pos]
   367	  have hR := integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI ha2
   368	  exact ⟨N2integrand_integrable μ hR alpha0 θ h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one hθ,
   369	    N2_outer_integrable μ hR alpha0 θ h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one hθ,
   370	    N1_integrable μ hI alpha0 θ h.alpha0_pos hθ (by linarith [h.threshold])⟩

   100	/-- The wave Green measure `G_s` on `ℝ^d` (main TeX lines 709, 5109-5113;
   101	Chen (2.5)): `d = 1`: `½ 1_{|x|<s} dx`; `d = 2`:
   102	`1_{|x|<s} dx / (2π√(s²-|x|²))`; `d = 3`: `σ_s/(4πs)`, written as
   103	`(s/(4π)) · map (ω ↦ sω) volume.toSphere`, which takes Mathlib's
   104	`Measure.toSphere` as the surface measure of the unit sphere (a definitional
   105	choice, Le's decision 4; see the module doc); other `d`: `0`. -/
   106	def waveGreen : (d : ℕ) → ℝ → Measure (Rd d)
   107	  | 1, s => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2) • volume.restrict (ball 0 s)
   108	  | 2, s => volume.withDensity ((ball (0 : Rd 2) s).indicator
   109	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹))
   110	  | 3, s => ENNReal.ofReal (s / (4 * π)) •
   111	      (volume.toSphere.map fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => s • (ω : Rd 3))
   112	  | _, _ => 0
   113	
   114	/-- Outside `d ∈ {1,2,3}` the definition is the zero measure (a convention;
   115	the manuscript has `d ∈ {1,2,3}`). -/
   116	theorem waveGreen_other (d : ℕ) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ 2) (h3 : d ≠ 3) (s : ℝ) :
   117	    waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   118	  unfold waveGreen; split <;> simp_all

   120	/-- For `s ≤ 0` the wave Green measure is zero (in `d = 1, 2` the ball is
   121	empty, in `d = 3` the factor `s/(4π)` is `≤ 0`). -/
   122	theorem waveGreen_of_nonpos (d : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : s ≤ 0) : waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   123	  by_cases h1 : d = 1
   124	  · subst h1; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   125	  by_cases h2 : d = 2
   126	  · subst h2; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   127	  by_cases h3 : d = 3
   128	  · subst h3
   129	    have : s / (4 * π) ≤ 0 := div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg hs (by positivity)
   130	    simp [waveGreen, ENNReal.ofReal_eq_zero.2 this]
   131	  exact waveGreen_other d h1 h2 h3 s

   175	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   176	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   177	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   178	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   179	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   180	\end{equation}
   181	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   182	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   187	\end{equation}
   188	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   189	
   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   191	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   198	  \]
   199	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215	
   216	Throughout we write
   217	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   218	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   219	\end{equation}
   220	
   221	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   222	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   223	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   224	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   225	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives

   232	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of

   234	stochastic interpretations or temporal covariances and do not supply this

   740	Write $G_\theta(s,y) = e^{-\theta s}G(s,y)$ and $\widehat{G}_s(\xi) =

   744	definitions, to distinguish it from the covariance measure:
   745	\begin{equation}\label{E:damped-norm-definitions}

   747	    N_0(\theta)&=\int_0^\infty e^{-\theta s}G_s(\R^d)\ud s,\\

   749	    \int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda

   755	  \end{split}
   756	\end{equation}

   766	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   767	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}

   770	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   771	  \[
   772	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   773	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   774	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   775	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   776	  \]
   777	  Let
   778	  \[
   779	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   780	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   781	  \]
   782	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   783	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   784	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   785	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   786	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   787	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   788	  \end{equation}
   789	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing, Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel, and
   790	  restriction of a temporal Laplace domain do not increase these corresponding
   791	  full or tail norm bounds.
   792	\end{lemma}

  5104	
  5105	\begin{proof}
  5106	  From Chen~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.5), p.~7}, the wave
  5107	  measures are
  5108	  \[
  5109	    G_h^{(2)}(\ud y)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\{|y|<h\}}\ud y}
  5110	    {2\pi\sqrt{h^2-|y|^2}},\qquad
  5111	    G_h^{(3)}(\ud y)=\frac{\sigma_h(\ud y)}{4\pi h},
  5112	  \]
  5113	  where $\sigma_h$ is surface measure on the sphere of radius $h$. Both have
  5114	  mass $h$ and satisfy $G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)$. Thus, the unsmoothed convolution is
  5115	  $ch^{1-\alpha}F_d(z/h)$, where $F_d(w) = \int G_1^{(d)}(\ud
  5116	  y)|y+w|^{-\alpha}$. In dimension three spherical coordinates give, for $\rho =
  5117	  |w| > 0$,
